risks.risk_description: Cyberattacks are expected to grow more aggressive and brazen, driven by increased remote/hybrid work, cloud technology reliance, and geopolitical tensions leading to state-sponsored hacking.

risk_driver.driver_description: Increased remote work provides opportunities for insiders to collude with hackers, increasing attack frequency.
Cloud providers are lucrative targets as breaches can expose multiple clients.
Adoption of new digital platforms without proper risk assessments increases vulnerabilities.
Conflicts such as the Ukraine invasion increase risks of state-sponsored cyberattacks.

risk_recommendations: Verify cloud service providers have appropriate controls to mitigate cyber risks.
Monitor frequency and nature of cyberattacks and implement mitigation measures.
Conduct background checks on employees with access to sensitive data.
Use software to detect inappropriate data access and data exfiltration attempts.
Utilize Dark Web scanning services to detect potential threats.
Provide cyber security training and conduct tabletop exercises for ransomware response.
risks.trend: Cyber security risks have been increasing over the past decade and are expected to continue growing more aggressive in 2024.
risks.likelihood: Almost certain (high likelihood) due to ongoing trends in remote work and geopolitical tensions.
risks.impact: Potential for severe disruptions, data theft, and reputational damage; impacts include operational disruption and financial loss.
risk_event: Increased cyberattacks since 2020 linked to remote work.
Ongoing risks from state-sponsored hacking related to Russia, China, and geopolitical conflicts.
suggested_audits: Information Security Policy and Procedure Audit
Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing Audit
Data Backup and Disaster Recovery Audit
contextual_variations: Public sector, major infrastructure, and organizations with large volumes of personal data are especially vulnerable.

risks.risk_description: Rapid adoption of generative AI tools like ChatGPT introduces risks including hallucinations, data privacy breaches, intellectual property theft, and sophisticated social engineering attacks.

risk_driver.driver_description: AI systems may produce incorrect or misleading outputs unpredictably.
Inputting sensitive data into AI tools risks privacy breaches and IP theft.
AI can be used to craft sophisticated social engineering attacks.

risk_recommendations: Maintain an inventory of AI-impacted technologies and processes.
Conduct risk assessments for AI implementations.
Engage third parties on their AI usage plans.
Define unacceptable AI uses.
Establish and enforce AI usage policies.
Validate AI outputs critically.
Monitor AI projects for risks and scalability.
risks.trend: AI technology is advancing rapidly and becoming pervasive, increasing both opportunities and risks.
risks.impact: Risks include suboptimal decisions due to AI bias, data theft, operational issues, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, plagiarism, and loss of competitive advantage.
suggested_audits: AI Training and Testing Data Audit
AI Incident Response and Contingency Audit

risks.risk_description: Stricter privacy regulations like Quebec's Law 25 increase compliance requirements and costs, requiring organizations to enhance data governance and transparency.

risk_driver.driver_description: New laws impose stricter data protection and transparency obligations.
Organizations must comply with varying privacy laws across regions.

risk_recommendations: Ensure private and confidential data is securely stored with adequate controls.
Understand applicable privacy laws and compliance requirements.
Map data storage and movement across systems and jurisdictions.
Assess data integrity during digital transitions.
Control third-party access to critical data.
Develop policies on AI tool usage and data management.
risks.trend: Privacy regulations are becoming more stringent and widespread, increasing organizational accountability.
risks.impact: Non-compliance risks include regulatory fines, reputational damage, and increased insider threats.
suggested_audits: Data Governance Policy and Procedures Audit
Data Governance Training and Awareness Audit
Data Governance Metrics and Reporting Audit
Data Governance Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Audit

risks.risk_description: Limited budgets and legacy systems challenge organizations to prioritize technology investments and maintain effective IT and operational technology governance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Limited resources may delay necessary upgrades and transformation.
Aging infrastructure increases risk and operational inefficiencies.
Unilateral technology decisions by departments can cause siloed risks.

risk_recommendations: Establish governance with cross-functional input for technology investment prioritization.
Set leadership tone to ensure timely infrastructure updates.
Implement processes to evaluate technology options considering risks and opportunities.
Vet third-party suppliers and manage related risks.
Conduct training and tabletop exercises for ransomware response.
risks.impact: Suboptimal IT/OT decisions can reduce control effectiveness, increase operational issues, and weaken security.
suggested_audits: IT/OT Incident Response and Business Continuity Audit
IT/OT Performance Measurement and Reporting Audit
IT/OT Budget and Resource Allocation Audit
IT/OT Documentation and Documentation Management Audit
IT/OT Cloud and Third-Party Services Audit

risks.risk_description: Increasing regulatory and societal expectations require organizations to proactively manage environmental, social, and governance responsibilities to avoid legal and reputational risks.

risk_driver.driver_description: ISSB standards and Canadian laws like Bill S-211 increase ESG compliance requirements.
Stakeholders demand greater accountability on environmental and social impacts.
Physical climate risks and social challenges like human trafficking require attention.

risk_recommendations: Set realistic and defendable ESG targets aligned with industry peers.
Assess impacts of inaction on ESG progress.
Ensure data integrity for ESG metrics.
Evaluate feasibility of targets and stakeholder perceptions.
Develop climate change mitigation and EDI strategies.
Enhance governance around emergency preparedness and social responsibility.
risks.trend: ESG regulation and focus are increasing, with growing emphasis on social and governance elements alongside environmental concerns.
risks.impact: Risks include rising compliance costs, physical climate impacts, social inequality, governance failures, and reputational damage.
suggested_audits: Climate Change Resilience and Adaptation Audit
Environmental Performance Monitoring and Measurement Audit
Supplier and Vendor Social Responsibility Audit
Social Accountability and Ethical Practices Audit
Social Performance Metrics and Reporting Audit
Code of Conduct and Ethics Audit
Succession Planning and Talent Management Audit

risks.risk_description: Growing reliance on third-party technology providers increases exposure to risks from vendor performance, security, compliance, and business continuity.

risk_driver.driver_description: Organizations outsource specialized IT functions due to labor shortages and cost considerations.
Includes contractors, consultants, and SaaS providers with network access.
Treating third-party risk management as a checkbox rather than ongoing review.

risk_recommendations: Conduct detailed risk assessments before contracting third parties.
Include risk mitigation accountability in contracts.
Incorporate third-party roles in business resilience and disaster recovery plans.
Test third-party response plans regularly.
Implement customized codes of conduct and cyber security training for third parties.
Regularly review and stress test third-party cyber security threat assessments.
risks.trend: Reliance on third parties for technology services is increasing, accelerating risk exposure.
risks.impact: Risks include cyber security breaches, fraud, quality issues, and system outages.
suggested_audits: Information Security and Data Privacy Audit
Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Audit
Third-Party Risk Assessment and Management Audit

risks.risk_description: M&A activities carry risks including financial mismanagement, fraud, cyber vulnerabilities, ESG exposures, and cultural misalignment that can impact deal success and valuation.

risk_driver.driver_description: Potential for financial mismanagement, pending litigation, and fraud.
Poor integration of digital platforms can expose organizations to cyberattacks.
Unaddressed ESG exposures and cultural conflicts can affect employee retention and investor expectations.

risk_recommendations: Include IT/OT controls, ESG, fraud, corruption, and cultural assessments in due diligence.
Define dealbreakers and no-go parameters clearly.
Conduct increased scrutiny on targets lacking risk management or internal audit functions.
Factor risk mitigation costs into valuation and integration planning.
risks.trend: M&A activity is increasing post-pandemic with heightened awareness of emerging risks.
risks.impact: Risks can lead to integration delays, cost overruns, loss of synergies, and reputational damage.
suggested_audits: Human Resources and Employee Benefits Audit

risks.risk_description: Accelerated digital transformation introduces risks related to cybersecurity, integration complexities, data quality, operational disruption, and workforce adaptation.

risk_driver.driver_name: Rapid Adoption of Cloud and Digital Platforms
risk_driver.driver_description: New platforms introduce new processes and potential cyber entry points.
Challenges in integrating new software with existing legacy systems.
Transformation impacts business models, human resources, and requires new skills.

risk_recommendations: Maintain an inventory of planned and completed digital changes.
Assess integration requirements with legacy systems.
Update controls, policies, procedures, and training post-transformation.
Plan for workforce training and resource needs.
Monitor changes in cyberattack patterns.
Evaluate realization of transformation benefits and lessons learned.
risks.trend: Digital transformation accelerated by the pandemic is ongoing, increasing exposure to related risks.
risks.impact: Risks include cybersecurity threats, data privacy issues, cost overruns, operational downtime, and resistance to change.
suggested_audits: User Experience and Customer Journey Audit

risks.risk_name: Data Analytics and Continuous Monitoring Risks
risks.risk_description: Increasing reliance on data analytics introduces risks related to data quality, governance, privacy, security, and ethical use.

risk_driver.driver_name: Rapid Growth in Data Volume and Sources
risk_driver.driver_description: Increased data from digitized processes and sensors requires robust management.
Risk of moving too fast or too slow in analytics maturity.

risk_recommendations: Regularly test data integrity and quality.
Ensure confidence in third-party data sources.
Validate accuracy of analytics outputs.
Monitor market share and customer feedback related to analytics.
Add analytics expertise at board and operational levels.
Develop and execute a data analytics maturity roadmap.
risks.trend: Analytics use has skyrocketed over the last decade and is now table stakes, with increasing focus on data quality.
risks.impact: Risks include loss of competitive advantage, poor decision-making, and internal audit redundancy.

risks.risk_description: Shifts in workforce demographics, remote work, and evolving employee expectations challenge organizations to attract, retain, and optimize critical talent.

risk_driver.driver_description: Baby boomer retirements and Gen Z's different work expectations.
Impact on corporate culture and management practices.
Smaller internal teams focused on supplier management.

risk_recommendations: Assess and support organizational culture and employee morale.
Provide competitive compensation, benefits, and development.
Plan for succession in critical roles.
Manage labor disruption risks.
Align incentive structures with desired behaviors.
Use AI and automation to support change management.
Monitor health and wellness, especially mental health.
risks.trend: Workforce transformation is ongoing with increasing volatility and challenges in retention and engagement.
risks.impact: Risks include talent shortages, decreased productivity, labor disruptions, and negative culture impacts.
suggested_audits: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Audit

risks.risk_description: Increasing frequency and severity of natural disasters and cyber incidents are driving up insurance costs, reducing coverage availability, and complicating claims.

risk_driver.driver_description: Record hurricanes, floods, wildfires, and droughts increase claims and costs.
Rising cyber incidents contribute to insurance claims and premiums.
Emerging AI risks may further affect insurance landscapes.

risk_recommendations: Understand overall risk landscape including natural disasters, cyber, and supply chain risks.
Decide which risks to absorb internally versus outsource to insurance.
Engage independent insurance advisors to optimize coverage and claims.
Monitor insurance renewals and claims closely.
risks.trend: Insurance is becoming less affordable and harder to access, with increasing claim complexities.
risks.impact: Risks include increased costs, uninsurable assets, denied claims, and financial exposure.

risks.risk_description: Economic uncertainty, inflation, and rising costs pressure business models, capital management, and consumer demand.

risk_driver.driver_description: Increased costs of living and borrowing impact households and businesses.
Uncertain if consumer demand will sustain or decline.
Organizations hesitant to invest or hire amid economic uncertainty.

risk_recommendations: Pressure test business models for resilience to economic scenarios.
Identify inefficiencies and underperforming areas.
Monitor trends, technologies, and consumer behavior shifts.
Manage cashflow to cover obligations.
Track success and risk metrics.
risks.trend: Economic challenges persist with fears of recession and ongoing inflationary pressures.
risks.impact: Risks include shrinking margins, low cash flow, reduced demand, increased costs, and supply chain constraints.
suggested_audits: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Audit
Supply Chain and Vendor Risk Audit

risks.risk_description: Organizations face increasing threats from pandemics, natural disasters, cyberattacks, and economic shocks requiring robust crisis preparedness and response.

risk_driver.driver_description: More frequent and severe crises shorten recovery times and increase vulnerability.
Dependence on third parties requires coordinated resilience planning.

risk_recommendations: Maintain and regularly update probable risk scenarios and response plans.
Conduct mock tabletop crisis scenarios with expert involvement.
Analyze past crisis responses to identify improvement areas.
Monitor peer crises to anticipate emerging threats.
Include third parties in resilience planning and training.
risks.trend: Crisis frequency and magnitude are increasing, emphasizing the need for preparedness.
risks.impact: Risks include operational disruption, safety issues, customer loss, and financial costs.

risks.risk_description: Capital projects carry high risks of cost overruns, timeline delays, quality issues, and safety concerns that can impact financial and operational performance.

risk_driver.driver_description: Rising labor and material costs increase project budgets.
Common errors can inflate project costs by 1-3%.
Poor quality can lead to downtime, maintenance, and reputational damage.
Lack of oversight can cause delays and cost overruns.

risk_recommendations: Use data analytics to detect billing inconsistencies.
Implement rigorous project management with inspections and status updates.
Conduct risk assessments during planning to identify design flaws and impacts.
Establish clear roles and responsibilities for delivery and oversight.
Include audit rights and dispute resolution in vendor contracts.
risks.impact: Risks include financial losses from overruns, safety incidents, legal issues, and quality concerns.
suggested_audits: Cost Control and Cost Estimation Audit
Quality Assurance and Quality Control Audit
Change Order and Variance Analysis Audit
Compliance with Regulatory and Legal Requirements Audit
Project Closure and Lessons Learned Audit

risks.risk_description: Economic pressures from rising cost of living increase fraud risk through elevated pressure and rationalization, compounded by opportunities from remote work and weak controls.

risk_driver.driver_description: Financial stress on employees increases motivation to commit fraud.
Remote work, incomplete policies, and poor training increase fraud opportunities.

risk_recommendations: Conduct regular fraud risk assessments.
Implement dual signatures for large transactions.
Use AI tools to monitor suspicious activities.
Restrict login access to minimum necessary individuals.
Provide fraud training and encourage reporting of suspicious behavior.
risks.trend: Fraud risk has increased due to economic conditions and remote work trends.
risks.impact: Risks include financial loss, legal penalties, business interruption, and reputational damage.
suggested_audits: Compliance with Code of Conduct and Ethics Policies Audit
Data Analytics for Fraud Detection Audit
